results.title: DualStream: Simultaneous desktop and mobile streaming, the easy way. | Product Hunt
results.content:
DualStream is one studio that streams to your Desktop and Mobile audiences at the same time - same sources, arranged for each scene, live everywhere in one click. The DualStream Relay - one upload from your PC, live on every platform from our servers. And if your connection drops mid-broadcast, Relay keeps every platform live on your standby screen and picks back up the moment you reconnect. Native Alerts, Per-Source audio control, VTuber support, instant replay clips (horizontal and vertical), cinema grade effects, pop-out multi-platform chat and so much more is all built in. [...] // MD & Tangent

Oh! Fun little P.S. ~ We also just released our first Open Source project for DualStream:An MCP server! This server lets AI assistants like Claude operate your DualStream studio: switch scenes, save instant-replay clips, build entire scene layouts from scratch, restyle your alerts and widgets, and react to what happens on stream. Everything runs locally on your machine, with your explicit approval, and every change renders on both your desktop and mobile canvases. Check it out here.

Omri Ben-Shoham [...] The app is free to download - build everything, test offline, go live to one channel. Premium is $9.99/month for access to the DualStream Relay, multi-format recording, water-mark free clips and streaming to more then one channel at a time.

🎁 For Product Hunt: use code PH-3M-HI6NIX at checkout and your first 3 months of Premium are free (or just go to dualstream.gg/ph, its applied automatically that way).  
  
We're a three-person team shipping every two weeks, and we genuinely build what users ask for. We'll all be here all day in the comments. Ask us anything, about the product, the build, the streaming category, the design process, the streamer feedback that shaped it, whatever. Genuinely grateful for your time!

// MD & Tangent

📌 [...] Hi, I made this. OpenVids is a desktop video editor where you describe what you want in chat and agents edit the timeline. A director agent splits the work between specialists (editor, vision, motion design, audio, research), and you watch the timeline change while they work. It's still a normal editor underneath, so you can fix things by hand. It's a fork of HeyGen's HyperFrames. There's no account and no cloud: you bring your own API key and the project is a folder of files on your machine. All your video projects live in one place, instead of being scattered across messy chats in Claude Code or Codex. Two things I built because the first version was bad: - Agents kept saying "done" on videos with black frames or dead audio. Now every prompt gets rendered and checked, and the agents fix [...] every prompt gets rendered and checked, and the agents fix what they find. - One bad prompt could wreck a project. Now every prompt is a checkpoint you can revert. Rough edges: builds aren't signed so your OS will complain on first launch. Chrome and FFmpeg are needed for rendering, but the first-run setup checks for them and installs what's missing. The demo video was made in the editor itself. It's early, so I'd love to hear what breaks on real footage.
